question.problem:
Find the median of the random variable $Y$ if the probability density function of $Y$ is given by

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}6{e}^{-6y},\, & y\ge 0, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The median of a random variable $Y$ is the number $m$ such that

$$
P(Y\le m)=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le m) & ={\int }_{0}^{m}6{e}^{-6y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{e}^{-6y}{|}_{0}^{m} \\  & =1-{e}^{-6m}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the median is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}1-{e}^{-6m} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ {e}^{-6m} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ -6m & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2}) \\ -6m & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ m & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
